main_text.p: quod quidem non substantiali forma est unum, sed duntaxat cotinuatione partium: cuius corporis partes tot simul sunt, quot prius in suis erant totis, quam permisceren tur, unaquæq; uidelicet sub pristina sua for ma. Sic igitur elementorum primis qualita tibus permistum, tantummodo fuerit ens unum sub pluribus formis cosistens. Quod profecto à natura corporis omnino alienū est. Nam multas actu formas, sub uno actu contineri non posse pluribus locis philoso phus ostendit. Et certe quodcunque unum est, non solummodo est unum propter extremorum continuationem, & purę contiguitatis priuatione, sed etiam propter actū, formamue, cuius ui fit, ut partes illę, ex quibus constat, unum fiant: alioqui enim eiusmodi corpus quidem tatummodo aceruus fuerit, uel potius uelut quædam ex Epicureis atomis compositio, aut ens terminorum continuatione, & non forma. Deinde Aristoteles eodem libro de Generatione et corruptione, non solas elementorum qualitates, sed & eorum substantias permisceri his uerbis satis aperte innuit. Ea (inquit) corpora commiscentur, quę similes inter se partes habet, & quæ postquam coaluerint, rursum

page.notes: Corrections: the printed text is in Latin with long s rendered as s; words broken at line ends were joined where the printed hyphen was absent or line-end hyphens restored where printed (e.g. "Ea (inquit)" and "Deinde" appear as printed). Doubtful readings: "permisceren tur" printed as split across lines; "tatummodo" likely printed "tantummodo" (printing error left as is in the scan appears as "tatummodo" at line 'aceruus'—copied as printed would be "tatummodo"); the sentence continues onto the next page ("rursum" is a catchword-like fragment at line end; kept in text). Printing errors left as printed: "unaquæq;", "sub pristina sua for ma" (hyphenated across lines), "tatummodo". The lower-left scan edge and the shadow at the page fold are not printed text and are omitted.
